scenarios.title: Lab smoke: owned queue, bounded send
scenarios.summary: Creates one owned anycast queue lab.<runId>.smoke on the verified lab broker and sends a bounded number of deterministic text messages to it, each with labRun and labSeq properties.
scenarios.expected: Fixture assertion: the queue's messageCount reaches the number sent before the readiness deadline. In Artemis Browser: the queue appears on /overview with that count, and /broker reports the node id the lab recorded. Cleanup removes exactly the queue and its address.

scenarios.title: Basic queues and connection
scenarios.summary: Five owned queues: empty (0); one (1 persistent); paged (251 persistent, seq 1..251); counters (12 sent, 3 consumed and acknowledged, 2 scheduled an hour out); and 'odd name & ü 日本', one message, for link encoding.
scenarios.expected: Fixture assertions: empty 0, one 1, paged 251; counters messageCount 9, scheduledCount 2, messagesAdded 12, messagesAcknowledged 3; odd name 1. In Artemis Browser: overview counters match, paged gives six pages at size 50 with one row on the last, scheduled messages are counted but not browsed, and the odd name links and escapes correctly. Delivering, expired and killed counts need held consumers and come with DELIVERY.

scenarios.title: Message bodies and export content
scenarios.summary: One queue, bodies, with 17 messages in labSeq order: plain text; Unicode, quotes, newline and literal HTML; empty and null text; bytes 0..63 and empty bytes; map; stream; object; one property of every type; 1,000-character text; 250,000-character text and 250,000 bytes (large messages); bodies and a note property starting =, +, - and @ with commas, quotes and newlines. Each carries labCase naming it.
scenarios.expected: Fixture assertion: messageCount 17. In Artemis Browser: each detail page matches its labCase; HTML shows as text; the two 250,000 messages carry large badges and bounded previews; exports parse, carry full supported bodies, and the CSV neutralises the four formula-like values. Compare with the run's send manifest.

scenarios.title: Filters, search and export bounds
scenarios.summary: search-a: 300 messages, marker='late' on 251-260 only (priority 0, so they browse last, at positions 291-300; every other message priority 1-9), odd seq persistent and even non-persistent, region eu/us, amount seq*3, distinct timestamps. search-b: 20, marker='late' on 5-8. search-many: 60, all marker='many' (over the 50-per-queue search cap). export-bounds: ten 400-character bodies, marker='deep' on 7-10.
scenarios.expected: Fixture assertions: the four counts, and by a whole-queue QueueBrowser marker='late' 10 and 4, marker='many' 60, marker='deep' 4, region='eu' AND amount>600 50. In Artemis Browser: the core filters marker = 'late', AMQPriority = 9, AMQDurable = 'NON_DURABLE' and region = 'eu' AND amount > 600 find exactly these; cross-queue search reports both late queues and a capped floor for search-many; exact-id lookups use ids from the send manifest.

scenarios.title: Scheduled, held, redelivered, dead-lettered and expired
scenarios.summary: sched: 5 waiting + 3 scheduled five minutes out. held: 20, a consumer (client lab-<run>-holder) holding 10 unacknowledged. all-held: 250, all held. imbalance: 20, one consumer holding 10 and one idle. redelivery: 3 messages, max 3 delivery attempts, dead-lettered to redelivery.dlq by the Roll back once step. expiry: 4 with a 2s TTL expiring to expiry.exp, 2 without. kill-none / kill-absent / kill-noqueue: one message rolled back to a limit of 2 with no dead-letter address, a missing one, and one with no queue; expire-none: one expiring with no expiry address.
scenarios.expected: Fixture assertions: sched 8 with 3 scheduled; held 20 with 10 delivering; all-held 250 delivering; imbalance 10 delivering on 2 consumers; redelivery 3; each kill variant 0 left and 1 killed; expiry 2 left and 4 expired, expiry.exp 4; expire-none 0 left and 1 expired. In Artemis Browser: scheduled and in-flight panels, empty browse with a non-empty queue, consumer imbalance (and, after ten minutes, age), redelivery counts between steps and the dead-lettered origin, killed/expired counters and Diagnose's explanation of where messages went. Acknowledge or release the held consumers from Workers and refresh.

scenarios.title: Routing, subscriptions and diverts
scenarios.summary: A01: anycast queue orders-q on address orders; multicast address feed with feed-sub-a and feed-sub-b. A02: multicast events with durable lab-<run>.durable-all (offline), durable filtered lab-<run>.durable-eu on region = 'eu' (drained), shared durable lab-<run>-shared and a live non-durable subscriber (a worker). A03: address routed with an exclusive divert of region = 'eu' to routed.eu and a non-exclusive divert to routed.audit; nowhere, a multicast address with no queue and auto-creation off.
scenarios.expected: Fixture assertions: orders-q 6, feed-sub-a 6, feed-sub-b 6; durable-all 10 with no consumer; durable-eu 0 left of 5 added, 5 acknowledged; shared 10; routed 3, routed.eu 3, routed.audit 3; nowhere 3 unrouted. In Artemis Browser: the address view groups each queue under its address, FQQN browsing reads every subscription, subscription kinds, filter and lag are shown, diverts link source to target, and the unrouted count appears on nowhere.

scenarios.title: Clients and rates
scenarios.summary: A04: queue clients with three idle clients kept as workers: producer lab-<run>-producer on 2 sessions, an anonymous consumer, consumer lab-<run>-consumer on 3 sessions. A05: queue rate, with steps to start a producer and a consumer at a chosen rate for a chosen time and to stop them. A06: a step that destroys and recreates rate, and Restart broker on the lab page.
scenarios.expected: Fixture assertion: clients has 4 consumers. In Artemis Browser: /broker, producer rows and /client pages identify each client with and without an id. Rates follow the lab's actual counts (the Workers panel) stage by stage; after Recreate rate queue or a broker restart, no negative or fabricated throughput is shown and a fresh baseline is needed.

scenarios.title: Queue behavior
scenarios.summary: Q01: idle (5, no client), browsed (5, only a browse-only client), paused (5, paused through management). Q02: lvq (last-value key k, 5 sends, 1 kept), ring (ring size 3, 10 sent, 3 kept). Q03: keep (non-destructive, 3 consumed and still 3), purge (purge on no consumers, no dead-letter address, 3 held by a consumer that leaves). Q04: exclusive (two consumers, all 20 to one), grouped (two consumers, groups g1/g2), gated (dispatch waits for 2 consumers, has 1).
scenarios.expected: Fixture assertions: idle 5 with no consumer; browsed 5, none delivering; paused 5 and paused; lvq 1 of 5 added; ring 3 of 10 added; keep 3, acknowledged 0; purge 0 left, 3 killed; exclusive 20 delivering on 2 consumers; grouped 20 delivering, 2 groups; gated 3 waiting, none delivering, 1 consumer. In Artemis Browser: effective settings and behavior findings explain each, and Diagnose tells no consumer, browse-only and paused apart. Steps resume and re-pause paused, and add gated's second consumer.

scenarios.title: Address pressure
scenarios.summary: page, fail, drop and block: each address limited to 20KB in 10KB pages under its policy, then sent 40 x 1KB (block's sender gives up after 5s). blocked: ample room, one message, blocked by an operator through management. Limits are on these addresses only.
scenarios.expected: Fixture assertions: page keeps all 40 and has pages; fail kept fewer than 40 and a send was refused; drop routed more than it kept; block kept fewer than 40; blocked is blocked via management. In Artemis Browser: usage beside policy with correct units, the observed operator block distinguished from inferred full-policy behaviour, and the observed block clearing after Unblock blocked.

scenarios.title: Global memory and disk thresholds
scenarios.summary: Needs a broker provisioned with Low global memory (global-max-size 2MB) or Disk threshold reached (max-disk-usage 1%). Low memory: queue memory gets 150 x 10KB. Disk: nothing is written to fill the disk; disk usage is read against the threshold and one persistent send to disk is tried.
scenarios.expected: Fixture assertions: low memory, global-max-size 2MB and address memory at least 50%; disk, usage above the 1% threshold (the send's outcome is recorded). In Artemis Browser: health shows global memory use and the disk threshold in the right units, and Diagnose reports the pressure.

scenarios.title: Permissions and interruption
scenarios.summary: Needs a broker provisioned with the Restricted users profile (management-message-rbac on). Creates queue failures with 5 messages and proves, as each test user, what the profile grants: viewer (password viewer) may manage but is refused the acceptors, disk usage, diverts, prepared transactions, roles and every address attribute; nomanage (password nomanage) may connect and is refused all management. E03 is Interrupt broker on the lab page: the broker goes down for chosen seconds and must come back as the same node.
scenarios.expected: Fixture assertions: failures 5; viewer lists queues; viewer is denied getAcceptorsAsJSON, diskStoreUsage and address attributes; nomanage is denied management. In Artemis Browser signed in as viewer: the denied panels say why and the rest still stand. As nomanage: the required failure is clear. During an interrupt: connection loss is explicit and a reconnect works.

scenarios.title: Read-only guarantee
scenarios.summary: Reads every queue this run owns (messages, delivering, scheduled, added, acknowledged, expired, killed) as a baseline. Use every Artemis Browser page on those queues, then Compare with baseline.
scenarios.expected: Compare finds no counter changed. Use a settled fixture: no traffic (refused while it runs), and nothing on a timer — a scheduled message falling due or a TTL shows as a change Browser did not cause.

scenarios.title: Scale and responsiveness
scenarios.summary: Queues x messages of small persistent bodies, from the form: 10 x 100 by default, up to 1,000 queues and lab.limits.max-scale-messages (100,000) in all. Combine with the other recipes for clients, subscriptions and held deliveries.
scenarios.expected: Fixture assertion: every queue holds its count. In Artemis Browser: overview, late-match filters, search, export, client and address pages stay responsive and correct; compare with the measured limits in .claude/memory.md.

scenarios.title: External harness: login, host, TLS and deployment
scenarios.summary: Not broker traffic: Browser profiles for loopback without login, configured login, hostile Host header, missing CSRF token, non-loopback startup, and the Helm deployment.
scenarios.expected: Documented as a harness procedure rather than a lab recipe.
